name: Qualcomm Incorporated

segments.note: Qualcomm reports segment earnings before taxes (EBT), not segment operating income. QSI and reconciling items are not shown.

footnotes: Qualcomm recorded a $4.2B income tax benefit in FY2026 (versus $7.1B of tax expense in FY2025), so net income exceeds pre-tax income; the flow chart shows pre-tax income flowing to net income.

Figures are from Qualcomm's FY2026 results (fiscal year ended Sep 27, 2026). Free cash flow = operating cash flow − capital expenditures (calculated). "Other" revenue is total revenue less QCT and QTL.
Percentages are of revenue; figures may not sum due to rounding.

summary: Qualcomm's revenue slipped 2.6% to $43.1B in fiscal 2026 (ended September 27, 2026) as handset chip revenue fell 13.4% to $24.1B. Automotive grew 51.7% to $6.0B and IoT 7.8% to $7.1B. Operating income fell 29.9% to $8.7B as R&D rose 12.9%.

Net income rose 2.5 times to $13.6B, or $12.70 per share, because a $4.2B tax benefit replaced a $7.1B tax charge the year before. Free cash flow fell 32.5% to $8.7B, and Qualcomm returned $11.7B through buybacks and dividends.
highlights: Automotive chip revenue reached a record $6.0B, up 51.7%.
Licensing (QTL) kept a 72% EBT margin on $5.6B of revenue.
watch: Handset chip revenue fell 13.4%, and Q1 FY2027 revenue is guided to $10.4B–$11.2B.
Net income was driven by tax swings, not operations.
Net debt rose to $7.4B as cash and securities fell 24.4%.

revenueLine.cap: Handsets fell 13.4% to $24.1B while automotive grew 51.7% to $6.0B.
revenueLine.say: Handset chip revenue fell 13.4 percent to 24.1 billion dollars, while automotive grew 51.7 percent to 6 billion.

spotlights.cap: Automotive revenue grew 51.7% to a record $6.0B as handsets declined.
spotlights.say: Automotive revenue grew 51.7 percent to a record 6 billion dollars, offsetting part of the decline in handsets.

spotlights.cap: Net income rose to $13.6B on a $4.2B tax benefit, though operating income fell 29.9%.
spotlights.say: Net income rose to 13.6 billion dollars thanks to a 4.2 billion dollar tax benefit, even though operating income fell 29.9 percent.
